title: the KEK passphrase from a root-only file or stdin, never the environment (F-45); one-time values in no log (7097514776)

findings.claim: the KEK passphrase given as sudo --preserve-env=TB_KEK_PASSPHRASE (the form install.sh, box-install.sh and RUNBOOK 16 showed) is logged by sudo with its value in the system journal, readable by root and the adm group (F-45); fixed: refused in the environment on every path, read only from a root-only 0600 file (removed once sealed) or stdin

tools/runbook_install.py's no-tpm lift gave the throwaway passphrase as -e TB_KEK_PASSPHRASE=<value> on docker exec's command line (the process list of the machine that runs it) and in the bootstrap's environment; fixed: written to a root-only file by stdin and named with --kek-passphrase-file

every box installed with the environment form before H-96 holds its passphrase in its journal and auth.log; the journal cannot drop single lines, so the passphrase is rotated (RUNBOOK 23, Rotate the KEK passphrase) and vacuuming the logs is hospital IT's decision
rc1 refuses tools.keys rotate-kek on a PRODUCTION box (R22-34, key_ceremonies), so a PRODUCTION box sealed under an exposed passphrase cannot rotate it under rc1; the page sends it to Aimedics

inside the box the adapter and the orchestrator would take TB_KEK_PASSPHRASE from the stack's environment and the audit signer is handed it by name (tools/trialbox/audit_heads.py PASSED); since H-96 nothing gives it a value and deploy/.env refuses it, but a value set by hand would sit in that container's configuration on disk (docker inspect), not in a log

the unit invariant cuts the steps between the signed re-run and the site keys (settings, compose, TLS) from its signed copy, so its deploy/.env check is empty there; the rehearsal job's install and reinstall phases run the whole path under the stand-in sudo, not run in this session (no Docker)

tests/unit/test_install_faults_runbook.py::test_installers_reject_passphrase_file_input is named for refusing a passphrase file; it still passes (it gives --passphrase-file, not --kek-passphrase-file) but its name now reads against the ruling

the first administrator's enrolment code and generated first password, printed by install.sh's accounts step on stdout, were kept by box-install.sh's tee in deploy/site/box/install.log and by the box rehearsal's step log, so anything that read the log held them (7097514776); fixed: shown once on a terminal (stdout only when it is one, else the controlling terminal), with no terminal in a root-only 0600 file under root's home that the output names, never in the output
findings.place: deploy/install.sh (5. accounts), deploy/box-install.sh (the install step's tee)

findings.claim: the first-run wizard's one-time code is written by box-install.sh show_code to stdout, which trialbox-firstrun.service sends to the journal (StandardOutput=journal+console), and outside WSL2 to /etc/issue.d for the screen, a file local users read; single use, voided after five wrong codes; not changed in this card

the rehearsal job uploads its step logs as an artifact for 30 days; before this card the install step's log held the throwaway rehearsal box's first password and enrolment code (synthetic, the box is removed after the run); since this card the values go to the box's root-only file

the passphrase file was checked by its name, one check at a time, and its folder never: another user who could write the folder could swap the file between the checks and the read (the review won 23 of 400 in the shell, 259 of 3000 in tools.keys), and a link put in place once kek.json appeared made shred -u empty any root file (review M-1 of #1398); fixed: the folders (real paths) root's and writable by no one else, the file opened once and checked and read on that descriptor, removed with rm; the race tests accept the other value 0 times

box-install.sh opened fd 8 with the passphrase on every install call, the file form too, and install.sh read and closed it only with --kek-passphrase-fd, so every child of the install inherited it (review L-1); fixed: fd 8 only for a passphrase from stdin, no copy of a file's value

the environment form is still honoured outside the paths this card names: libs/tb_common/kek.py load_kek, tools/trialbox/audit_heads.py PASSED (docker run -e by name), tools/trialbox/backup_schedule.py (review L-2); card H-97's
the host check's no-TPM line became a WARN on the back end's name alone (review L-3); ruled (7102655419): a listed WARN on a PoC box only (D-1091), a FAIL elsewhere; done
